title: Preventive Maintenance Agreements — Writing Down Arrears for Visits the Office Never Performed
content:
## Contract administration ruling

The instalment arrears carried into a settlement of a Preventive Maintenance Agreements record are written down for the visits the office booked and never performed. A booking the office attended and closed as a no-access call is taken as answered for this purpose, since the office attended, and does not count as a visit the office never performed.

The value written off per visit is the annual price in force divided by the visits the term credited.

### The ladder

| Booked visits of the agreement standing with no visit completed against them | The instalment arrears |
|---|---|
| 2 or more | the instalments invoiced less every payment received, less the value of each of those visits, taken as the annual price in force divided by the visits the term credited |
| exactly 1 | the instalments invoiced less every payment received, less half of that value |
| none — every booked visit has been answered by a completed visit | the instalments invoiced on the agreement less every payment received on it |

### Worked cases (hypothetical figures)

An agreement whose annual price in force is 4 800.00 USD, whose term credited 8 visits, with 6 000.00 USD of instalments invoiced and 4 500.00 USD of payments received. The value of one visit is 4 800.00 USD divided by 8, that is 600.00 USD.

- With 3 booked visits standing unanswered: 1 500.00 USD less 3 multiplied by 600.00 USD, that is 1 500.00 USD less 1 800.00 USD, which falls below nothing and so leaves arrears of nothing.
- With exactly 1 booked visit standing unanswered: 1 500.00 USD less half of 600.00 USD, that is 1 500.00 USD less 300.00 USD, leaving 1 200.00 USD.
- With every booked visit answered: 1 500.00 USD.
- A booking closed as a no-access call counts as answered, so an agreement whose only unanswered booking was closed that way is read in the last row.
